items.t: Ping An stock takes on regional role as APEC sponsor
sum: Ping An was named an official sponsor of APEC 2026 on November 12, with the group set to provide insurance protection and financial, healthcare and technology services for meetings in Shenzhen. The announcement was made in a Ping An release carried by AAP News.

The planned insurance program covers approximately 60 million US dollars and includes personal accident, public liability and property risks. Ping An also plans cross-border payment, healthcare and travel support for international visitors, extending the group's integrated finance and health-care strategy into a major regional event.

On the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, Ping An closed at 43.80 CNY on Friday, November 13, down 3.14 percent from 45.22 CNY on Friday, November 6. The comparison uses the closing prices of the same Hong Kong-listed instrument and places the week's market performance alongside the new APEC role.

sum: Ping An reported resilient underlying performance for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as operating profit advanced while the group expanded artificial intelligence across its financial and healthcare businesses. The company announced the results on October 28 in a Ping An results release.

Operating profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company increased 8.3 percent year on year to RMB125,905 million in the first nine months. Equity attributable to shareholders of the parent company reached RMB1,044,366 million at September 30, up 4.4 percent from the end of 2025.

Life and health insurance operating profit rose 5.7 percent to RMB87,238 million. Ping An P&C increased premium income 3.5 percent to RMB265,215 million, while its combined ratio improved by 1.4 percentage points to 95.6 percent. The bank also contributed to the result: revenue rose 2.4 percent to RMB103,100 million and net profit increased 2.2 percent to RMB39,186 million.

Ping An said its Express Service enabled AI-supported inquiry, consultation and processing in 90 percent of the group's business scenarios by September 30. The service had handled more than 150 million user sessions and resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI.

Average daily token consumption exceeded 330 billion in September, more than ten times the December 2025 level. Token output per compute unit increased 509 percent, while cost per token declined 81 percent. The company presented these changes as support for scalability and efficiency, rather than as a standalone explanation for earnings.

AI Doctor served users more than 62 million times in the first nine months, and AI service representatives handled about 1,484 million interactions, equal to 82 percent of total customer service volume. Smart fraud detection generated RMB10.04 billion in claims savings for Ping An P&C, 9.7 percent more than a year earlier.

For investors, the results underline the difference between recurring operating progress and the sensitivity of reported performance to investment markets. Ping An said its insurance funds investment portfolio grew 5.2 percent from the start of the year to RMB6.83 trillion at September 30.

Ping An Bank stock: Q3 report shows revenue and profit growth
sum: Ping An Bank released its third-quarter report on October 24, covering the nine months ended September 30, 2026. A WallStreetCN report published by Futu said operating income rose 2.4 percent year over year to RMB 103.1 billion, while net profit attributable to shareholders increased 2.2 percent to RMB 39.186 billion.

Net interest income reached RMB 66.755 billion, up 0.3 percent from the same period a year earlier. The report said the third-quarter net interest margin reached 1.80 percent, supported by lower funding costs and efforts to improve the corporate liability mix.

Corporate loan balances stood at RMB 1.709026 trillion at the end of September, while corporate deposits reached RMB 2.386713 trillion. The average interest rate on corporate deposits for the first nine months fell to 1.28 percent, indicating progress in funding-cost management even as loan growth remained moderate.

Retail customers totaled 130.2789 million at the end of September, and retail assets under management rose to RMB 4,392.327 billion. Personal loans were more uneven: mortgage balances increased, while credit-card receivables, consumer loans and business loans declined from year-end levels.

The report also highlighted new artificial-intelligence-enabled card products and expanded digital service tools. For investors, the development points to Ping An Bank's effort to deepen customer engagement beyond traditional lending and deposit products.

The non-performing loan ratio was 1.05 percent at the end of September, unchanged from year-end 2025, while the loan-loss reserve coverage ratio stood at 214.75 percent. The corporate-loan non-performing loan ratio was 0.89 percent, compared with 1.20 percent for personal loans.
Ping An Bank is a Shenzhen-headquartered commercial bank serving individual consumers, companies, interbank partners and small businesses across China.

sum: Ping An Insurance reported stronger underlying earnings for the first nine months of 2026, with operating profit rising despite pressure on investment performance. In a results release dated Wednesday, October 28, the company said operating profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company increased 8.3 percent year on year to RMB125,905 million for the period ended September 30. The official Ping An release also reported a 4.4 percent year-to-date increase in equity attributable to shareholders of the parent company.

Life and health insurance remained the main operating-profit contributor. Its operating profit rose 5.7 percent year on year to RMB87,238 million. In property and casualty insurance, premium income grew 3.5 percent to RMB265,215 million, while the combined ratio improved by 1.4 percentage points to 95.6 percent. A lower combined ratio indicates stronger underwriting performance because claims and related costs consumed a smaller share of premiums.

Ping An Bank added to the group's operating base. Revenue increased 2.4 percent year on year to RMB103,100 million in the first nine months, while net profit rose 2.2 percent to RMB39,186 million. The bank's non-performing loan ratio stood at 1.05 percent at September 30, and its core tier 1 capital adequacy ratio rose 0.25 percentage points year to date to 9.61 percent.

The insurance group's investment portfolio reached RMB6.83 trillion at the end of September, up 5.2 percent from the start of the year. Ping An said its 10-year average net investment yield was 4.8 percent and its 10-year average comprehensive investment yield was 4.9 percent. These long-term figures provide context for the group's effort to balance short-term market swings with recurring insurance and banking earnings.

Technology was another focus of the update. Ping An said its Express Service supported AI-enabled inquiry, consultation and processing in 90 percent of the group's business scenarios by September 30. The service had been used more than 150 million times and resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI, according to the company.
AI service representatives handled about 1,484 million interactions in the first nine months, equal to 82 percent of total customer service volume.

sum: Ping An Insurance reported a mixed nine-month performance for the period ended September 30, 2026. In a results release carried by etnet, the insurer said operating profit attributable to shareholders rose 8.3 percent year on year to 125.905 billion yuan.

Reported net profit moved in the opposite direction. Reuters reported that net profit declined 27.3 percent year on year, as investment income fell amid a volatile Chinese stock market. A separate market report put investment income at 49.49 billion yuan, down 68.6 percent, highlighting the sensitivity of headline earnings to portfolio performance.

Life and health insurance operating profit increased 5.7 percent to 87.238 billion yuan. That resilience was offset by a 13.3 percent decline in new business value to 30.99 billion yuan, a closely watched measure of the future profitability of newly written policies.

Property and casualty operations also supported the underlying result. Ping An said smart fraud detection generated claims savings of 10.04 billion yuan in the first nine months, an increase of 9.7 percent from a year earlier. The figures point to continued efficiency gains, while weaker new business value remains a challenge for future growth.

Ping An continued to push its AI in ALL strategy. AI-enabled inquiry, consultation and processing covered 90 percent of the group's business scenarios by September 30. AI service representatives handled about 1.484 billion interactions, representing 82 percent of total customer service volume.

The company also said Express Service resolved 91 percent of customer requests end to end with AI, while 95 percent of life insurance policies were underwritten within seconds. Those applications may help control costs and improve service capacity, but the earnings release does not establish that the technology alone caused the reported profit performance.

items.t: Insurance Partnership Could Shape What Comes Next For WeRide Stock
sum: WeRide announced a global insurance partnership program with Allianz Insurance Singapore and Ping An Property & Casualty to support autonomous driving services across existing operations in China, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, as well as planned launches in Europe, with coverage spanning liability, product risks, privacy and cybersecurity.

The initiative targets full lifecycle insurance for WeRide’s roughly 3,600 autonomous vehicles, including more than 1,800 Robotaxis. It aims to streamline risk coverage across markets and support unit economics as deployments scale through platforms such as WeRide Go, Uber and TXAI.
We will examine how WeRide’s investment narrative is influenced by this global insurance partnership program that targets lifecycle coverage for L4 fleets.

To own WeRide, you need to believe large scale L4 fleets can move from heavy investment to more self funded growth. The global insurance partnership speaks directly to that thesis. It targets consistent coverage across roughly 3,600 autonomous vehicles, which could help shorten deployment lead times and support the push for higher vehicle utilization in more cities.

The immediate catalyst still sits with new fully driverless permits and proof that Abu Dhabi style economics travel into other high fare markets. The biggest near term risk remains cash burn from R&D and expansion if ride volumes, pricing or partner demand through platforms like Uber and TXAI do not line up with that larger fleet footprint.

The new global insurance program is tightly linked to those permitting and utilization catalysts. Allianz Insurance Singapore and Ping An bring local expertise in multiple jurisdictions, which may simplify how WeRide structures liability, product, privacy and cybersecurity coverage as it moves from pilot zones to broader city operations in China, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

Framing this against the rest of the story, investors are watching whether these insurance structures reduce friction for regulators and mobility partners and make it easier to run a dense network of robotaxis and robobuses. Execution around pricing, loss experience and claims handling will matter because high insurance costs or coverage gaps could offset the benefits and keep unit economics under pressure.

Ping An stock gains a new AI governance test for investors
sum: Ping An Bank has formalized board-level oversight of artificial intelligence, adding a governance layer as automated tools expand across compliance and operational reviews. The policy was disclosed on September 30, 2026, and The Asian Banker reported the framework on October 9.

The board strategy committee will coordinate AI development and application management. The framework covers data security, algorithm risk, ethical review and accountability across the technology lifecycle.

The additional governance detail is that Ping An Bank said the policy implements guidance issued by China's National Financial Regulatory Administration in June. AI risks are incorporated into comprehensive risk management and classified by risk level, linking board responsibility to applications already used in control functions.

Ping An Bank's interim report recorded more than 450 large-model use cases by June and 140 operational-review agents across 55 scenarios. The applications include anti-money-laundering due diligence and account review.

For investors, the policy moves the question beyond adoption toward execution. Formal oversight may help contain data, model and accountability risks, but the policy alone does not establish a financial return from the deployments. The next test is whether Ping An converts broader AI use into measurable efficiency while preserving control quality.

Ping An stock traded at 6.07 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:35 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The latest relevant prior report cited 6.07 euros on Thursday, November 5, at 15:35 CET, so the new governance detail, rather than a price move, is the main change in this update.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 237 points, or 0.93 percent, to 25,413 points, delivering a full-day market turnover of HK$209 billion.
Chip makers continued their rally, with Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor (1347) advancing 4.92 percent and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (0981) rising 1.64 percent.

Tech heavyweights delivered mixed performances. Baidu (9888) and Xiaomi (1810) extended their losses, falling 4.69 percent and 3.31 percent, respectively. Xiaomi is set to unveil new foldable smartphones and other products this evening. Meituan (3690) slid 2 percent, while JD.com (9618) edged 1.45 percent lower. Tencent (0700) and Alibaba (9988) slipped 0.99 percent and 0.45 percent, respectively.
BYD Electronics surged 6.84 percent to top the blue-chip gainers, followed by Li Auto (2015), which rose 5.4 percent. In contrast, Geely Auto (0175) fell 2.84 percent.

Insurance and banking stocks came under pressure after five state-owned insurers and three banks announced plans to raise up to 360 billion yuan (HK$420.61 billion) through capital injections from the Ministry of Finance and other shareholders. items.t: Ping An unveils AI solutions in healthcare, insurance, payments at WAIC 2026
sum: Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. showcased AI innovations at WAIC 2026, targeting healthcare, insurance, and payments. Highlights include a disease-specific AI portfolio, 100% AI coverage in P&C operations, and a financial AI assistant for 251 million users. The moves reinforce its strategy to integrate finance with health and senior care services.

Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. unveiled a range of innovative artificial intelligence (AI) products and services at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference 2026 (WAIC 2026). Spanning healthcare, insurance, and payments scenarios, these innovations further advance the AI-driven development of Ping An's "integrated finance + health and senior care" strategy. The Group's initiatives aim to enhance service efficiency and customer experience across its ecosystems.

Ping An's latest healthcare AI applications focus on complex disease diagnosis, treatment, and everyday health management. The Group launched its first "disease-specific AI product portfolio" for patients with cancer and other critical illnesses. This portfolio includes disease prediction services, disease-specific insurance, and the Peking University Healthcare AI Disease Manager. These offerings connect disease risk identification, insurance protection, and professional healthcare services.

For everyday health management, the "AI Family Doctor" from Ping An Healthcare and Technology Company Limited serves 90 million monthly active users. The service uses an "AI + Physician" model, where AI handles high-frequency needs such as consultation triage and medication reminders, while physicians manage complex conditions. Ping An's AI Doctor supports accurate diagnosis across more than 11,300 diseases and serves nearly 12 million users annually.

Ping An Property & Casualty has achieved 100% AI coverage across its core business scenarios, improving overall operational efficiency by 80%. AI now empowers the entire insurance value chain, including services, marketing, operations, and business management.

Ping An Bank, UnionPay, and Tencent Launch China's First "AI Compute Card," Shifting Bank Card Rewards from Gift Points to LLM Compute Power
sum: Competition in bank card rewards is shifting from traditional point-based gift exchanges and airline miles toward the more tech-forward appeal of large language model (LLM) compute power. On June 30, Ping An Bank, together with China UnionPay and Tencent Cloud, officially launched China's first debit card designed for personal AI compute consumption—the "AI Compute Card." The product directly links users' daily payment behavior with AI productivity, signaling that financial institutions are beginning to participate deeply in the push to make AI accessible to the masses. The move aims to lock in younger customers and digital productivity workers through "compute-power rewards" in an era of fierce competition for market share.

According to a report by China Business News (CBN), the card integrates three core functions: aggregated compute-power payments, basic financial services, and exclusive compute-power rewards. Cardholders accumulate compute-power points according to set rules through card spending or by reaching certain asset tiers, creating an experience where "using the card accumulates compute power." Applications for the card will gradually open in July through Ping An Bank's Pocket Bank app and offline branches. Ping An Bank also plans to launch a credit card under the same theme in July, forming a product matrix that links debit and credit functions.

In this collaboration, the three parties have clearly defined roles, jointly building a closed loop from compute infrastructure to front-end applications. China UnionPay provides the cloud computing platform and an aggregated entry point for AI large language models. Tencent Cloud supplies AI office and learning tools centered on WorkBuddy. Ping An Bank is responsible for the account system, customer operations, and financial service integration.

UnionPay's cloud computing platform has completed the private deployment and aggregated access to multiple mainstream AI large language models, building a secure and controllable compute resource pool. Users no longer need to repeatedly register, top up, or switch between multiple AI platforms.

items.t: Merdeka Gold Debuts in Hong Kong in Indonesia’s First Dual Listing in Over 20 Years
sum: Jakarta. Merdeka Gold Resources (EMAS) began trading on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Friday through a Hong Kong Depositary Receipts (HDR) listing, marking the first dual listing by an Indonesian company in Hong Kong in more than two decades.
The company's HDRs started trading at 9:30 a.m. Hong Kong time at an offer price of HK$26.60 per HDR, with each board lot consisting of 100 HDRs.

The listing represents a milestone both for Merdeka Gold Resources and Indonesia's capital market, becoming the first Indonesian issuer to secure a dual listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in over 20 years. It is also the first HDR listing in Hong Kong in more than a decade.
President Director Boyke Poerbaya Abidin said the secondary listing would broaden the company's access to international investors while raising its profile in global capital markets.
"The successful listing on HKEX marks an important milestone for Merdeka Gold Resources and strengthens Indonesia's presence in global capital markets," Boyke said on Friday.

"The transaction provides wider access for international investors to gain exposure to one of Indonesia's most significant gold growth assets and reflects confidence in the quality of the Pani Gold Project."
The company expects the dual listing to expand its investor base, improve global visibility, and support its next phase of growth.

items.s: Beansprout - Singapore’s Leading Financial Insights Platform - Growbeansprout.com
sum: I look at 3 SGX dividend ETFs that help to diversify income across ASEAN, Asia Pacific financials and China dividend stocks.
This post was created in partnership with SGX. All views and opinions expressed in this article are Beansprout's objective and professional opinions.
The STI has reached new highs in recent months, supported by gains in Singapore blue chips.
For investors who already own Singapore banks, REITs and blue-chip stocks, this has helped portfolio returns.
At the same time, stronger share prices can also moderate dividend yields if dividends do not rise at the same pace.
Investors who already own Singapore dividend stocks in their investment portfolio may be looking at ways to further diversify their income stream.
In this article, I look at three SGX-listed dividend ETFs that provide exposure to ASEAN dividend stocks, Asia Pacific financials and China dividend companies.

Ping An Reports Steady 7.6% Growth in Operating Profit Attributable to Shareholders of the Parent Company in Q1 2026, Life & Health NBV Increases 20.8% YoY
sum: HONG KONG and SHANGHAI, April 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. (hereafter "Ping An" or the "Group"; HKEX: 2318; SSE: 601318) today announced its first quarter financial results for the three months ended March 31, 2026.

2026 marks the commencement of China's 15th Five-Year Plan. Despite a complex and volatile external environment and challenges to economic performance, China's economy made a good start in the first three months of 2026. Ping An remains committed to its core financial business while consistently advancing its "integrated finance + health and senior care" strategy and upgrading services to build a differentiated core competitive advantage. The Group achieved steady overall operations and high-value growth in core businesses, demonstrating the resilience of development.

The Group's operating profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company grew 7.6% year on year to RMB40,780 million in the first three months of 2026. The Group's equity attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB1,018,310 million, up 1.8% from the beginning of the year as of March 31, 2026. Total assets rose above RMB14 trillion to approximately RMB14.17 trillion as of March 31, 2026. Life and health insurance ("Life & Health") business achieved significant progress in high-quality development. In the first three months of 2026, Life & Health's first-year premium ("FYP") increased by 45.5% to RMB66,340 million. New business value ("NBV") climbed 20.8% year on year to RMB15,574 million. Bancassurance, community finance and other channels' share in Ping An Life's NBV increased by 6.8 pps year on year. The integrated financial service model improved the efficiency of customer development. As of March 31, 2026, Ping An's retail customers increased 0.2% from the beginning of the year to nearly 252 million. The retention rate of customers holding products across three or more product lines was 99% in the 12 months ended March 31, 2026. The advancing health & senior care strategy enabled core businesses via differentiation. The QR code payment service covered 111 thousand pharmacies nationwide, and cumulatively over 290 thousand customers had become entitled to home-based senior care services as of March 31, 2026.

HONG KONG and SHANGHAI, March 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. (hereafter "Ping An" or the "Group", HKEX: 2318; SSE: 601318) today announced its financial results for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Despite a complex and volatile macroeconomic environment in 2025, the strong resilience of China's economy and the fundamental momentum of structural upgrade provided solid foundations for Ping An to overcome challenges and grow steadily. Ping An consistently advanced its "integrated finance + health and senior care" strategy, sharpened its core competitive edge via "service differentiation", and delivered results characterized by positive trends, high-value growth, strategic advancement, and service innovation.
- Operating profit after tax attributable to shareholders of the parent company was RMB134,415 million, up 10.3% year on year.
- Net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company excluding non-recurring gains and losses was RMB143,773 million, up 22.5% year on year.
- Equity attributable to shareholders of the parent company exceeded RMB1 trillion for the first time, totaling RMB1,000,419 million, up 7.7% from the beginning of 2025.

- Attaching great importance to shareholder returns, Ping An plans to pay a final dividend of RMB1.75 per share in cash for 2025. Total cash dividends paid for 2025 will be RMB48,891 million, having risen for 14 consecutive years.

China ETF News: Alibaba, JD, & Meituan Rocket On “The Takeout War Is Over”
sum: Asian equities had a strong day on the hope that Middle East tensions are simmering down.

Let’s not bury the lead: Mainland media source, the Economic Daily, which describes itself as the “official outlet for the government to publicize its economic policies,” published an article titled “The Takeout War is Over.” This article outlines the toll that the restaurant delivery war has taken on drivers, merchants, and the balance sheets and market capitalizations of Meituan, JD.com, and Alibaba. Yesterday, we noted that the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation met with 12 internet companies, including Alibaba’s Taobao, Trip.com, Meituan, JD.com, ByteDance’s Douyin, and Kuaishou, regarding the ongoing delivery price wars. This declaration appears to be the direct result of those meetings.

Additionally, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) held a symposium yesterday on “price supervision and anti-unfair competition.” In a press release, SAMR stated “Price supervision and competition work should focus on building a strong domestic market,” and efforts should be made to “thoroughly rectify involutionary competition." Instant commerce subsidies have weighed significantly on companies' bottom lines, as adjusted net income and adjusted EPS have both cratered.

Equity strategists are stuck focusing on the MSCI China Index and earnings per share (EPS). The overall EPS level for the members of the MSCI China Consumer Discretionary Index has been decimated by Alibaba’s 39% weight and its EPS decline in 2025, as well as Meituan, which is 8% of the index, and JD.com, which is 4.7% of the index. One caveat is that Alibaba’s artificial intelligence (AI) capex has also been a factor in the steep fall in EPS. Ultimately, the restaurant delivery and instant commerce price war has affected investors’ perception of China investing, both explicitly through the individual companies' EPS declines and implicitly through the knock-on effect of strategists who focus on MSCI China EPS.

Meituan gained +13.92% on volume that increased +466% from yesterday, which is 5X the 1-year average. Alibaba gained +4.63% on volume up +70% from yesterday, though its Hong Kong stock had several big put trades, and JD.com gained +4.85% on volume up +124% from yesterday.

items.t: China ETF News: Mainland Investors Buy Hong Kong Stocks On Weakness
sum: Asian equities were lower overnight on President Trump’s threat to escalate Iranian military efforts, as higher oil prices and central banks potentially pivoting to higher, not lower, interest rates in 2026 raised stagflation and inflation shock fears. Pakistan was closed for Pakistan Day, celebrating the country’s birth in 1956, and Indonesia was closed for the "Idul Fitri" Festival that marks the end of Ramadan.

This morning’s Trump claim of Iranian talks sent futures higher. Both Hong Kong and Mainland China sold off on high volumes, as the Hang Seng Index closed below the 25,000 level, while Mainland China had only 288 advancing stocks versus 4,866 declining stocks.

We often point to insurance giant AIA, which fell -7.79% overnight, as a proxy for foreign professional sentiment. The stock is not part of the MSCI China Index, which is part of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index. Rather, it is part of the MSCI Hong Kong Index, which is considered a developed market benchmark. The sharp drop in the insurer's stock indicates a rush by foreign professional investors to exit positions regardless of price.

Premier Li’s keynote speech at the China Development Forum in Beijing included a commitment to China’s continued opening up and willingness to address trade concerns. This year’s event is titled "China During the 15th Five-Year Plan Period: High-Quality Development & tThe Joint Creation of New Opportunities". Interestingly, Apple’s Tim Cook is the international co-chair for the Forum this year. China's central bank governor Governor Pan also spoke at the Forum, reiterating “loose monetary policy” and willingness to lower interest rates. Vice Premier He Lifeng spoke yesterday to at the US China Business Council

The Beijing city government called in a group of E-Commerce heavyweights that included Alibaba, Meituan, and JD.com, to discuss the extreme competition thatr erupted last year in the instant commerce, i.e. the delivery of goods, both food and non-food, in thirty minutes or less to urban consumers. I view this as a positive signal for the companies' bottom lines as consumer subsidies were weighing heavily on profitability, which was reflected in Alibaba's earnings last week.

SGX launches three new Hong Kong SDRs including Zijing Gold
sum: Zijin Gold, China's largest gold producer, offering exposure to gold's momentum and rising investor interest in precious metals

SGX is introducing Singapore Depository Receipts of three Hong Kong stocks starting from Feb 2. With these additions, SGX Stock Exchange now offers 32 SDRs across China, Hong Kong, Thailand, and Indonesia.

The three new Hong Kong SDRs are Zijin Gold (HZGD) – China's largest gold producer, offering exposure to gold's momentum and rising investor interest in precious metals; Horizon Robotics (HHZD) – China's leader in AI computing and autonomous driving solutions, partnering with major automakers and powering China's smart mobility transition and China Mobile (HCMD) – China's largest mobile network operator and a key player in AI-driven digital infrastructure, offering attractive dividend yields.

According to SGX, the launch of these three new SDRs rides on strong growth momentum in the SDR market, which has seen a remarkable 10X year-on-year growth in daily turnover to $12 million across 29 underlyings from 3 markets.

"The steady expansion of underlyings into diverse sectors – from growth technology stocks to defensive financials and digital infrastructure plays – continues to broaden diversification opportunities for investors," says SGX.
Existing Hong Kong SDRs are PetroChina, Bank of China, Xiaomi, Ping An Insurance, Alibaba, HSBC, Meituan, Baidu, BYD, JD.com, Tencent, Pop Mart, CATL, Laopu Gold and Trip.com.
According to SGX, the existing Hong Kong SDRs enjoyed $150 million in net retail inflows in 2025, suggesting "robust interest".

items.t: Amid low rates, UOB Asset Management launches dividend-focused ETF aiming to pay 6%
sum: The new fund invests in ‘leading companies’ in Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines
[SINGAPORE] With rates steadily falling over the past year, investors might be on the lookout for higher-yielding assets to put their money in.
T-bill yields fell below the 2 per cent mark in the second half of 2025 amid a globally lower rate regime.
But certain assets are still offering higher yields, such as income-focused funds, bond funds and real estate investment trusts.
UOB Asset Management is launching one such dividend-focused fund: the UOBAM Ping An FTSE Asean Dividend Index ETF.

The firm said on Wednesday (Jan 7) that this is the only dividend-focused Asean exchange-traded fund (ETF) to be listed on the Singapore Exchange (SGX). It is also part of the Singapore Exchange-Shenzhen Stock Exchange ETF Product Link.
The UOBAM Ping An FTSE Asean Dividend Index ETF aims to pay dividends of at least 6 per cent in 2026 and 2027, which UOB Asset Management said is one of the highest among Singapore-listed ETFs.

items.t: Hong Kong stocks slide after China’s economic data shows growth running out of steam
sum: Hong Kong stocks fell by the most in three weeks on Monday after key economic data showed China’s slowdown extended into November, keeping investors on edge over the sustainability of a nearly 30 per cent market rally this year.

The Hang Seng Index closed 1.3 per cent lower at 25,628.88, its steepest drop since November 21. The Hang Seng Tech Index slumped 2.5 per cent. On the mainland, the CSI 300 Index and the Shanghai Composite Index both lost 0.6 per cent.

Drug makers led the declines as Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group slumped 7.6 per cent to HK$39.74 and Innovent Biologics tumbled 4.1 per cent to HK$81.75. Chinese search engine operator Baidu slid 5.8 per cent to HK$118.70 and short-video platform operator Kuaishou Technology declined 4.5 per cent to HK$64.45. Alibaba Group Holding fell 3.6 per cent to HK$148.60.
